To solve this problem, we need to consider the concept of time dilation in special relativity.

  From your perspective, you are traveling at the speed of light, which means you are experiencing time dilation. Time dilation is the phenomenon where time appears to pass more slowly for an observer in motion relative to a stationary observer.

  Since you are traveling at the speed of light, you are experiencing time dilation. From your perspective, time is passing normally, but from the perspective of the child, time is passing more slowly due to your high-speed motion.

  Let's assume that the child is born at time t = 0 from your perspective. From the child's perspective, time is passing normally, so the child would be 1 year old when you leave.

  As you travel towards the child at the speed of light, time dilation becomes more pronounced. From the child's perspective, time is passing normally, but from your perspective, time is passing more slowly due to your high-speed motion.

  Since you are traveling at the speed of light, you are experiencing time dilation by a factor of 1 / sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2), where v is your velocity and c is the speed of light. In this case, v = c, so the time dilation factor is 1 / sqrt(1 - 1) = infinity.

  This means that from your perspective, time is standing still. You are essentially frozen in time, and you will not experience any aging during your journey.

  From the child's perspective, however, time is passing normally. The child will continue to age at a rate of 1 year per year, so when you arrive, the child will be 1 year old + the time it took you to travel, which is still 1 year.

  Therefore, from the child's perspective, you will arrive when the child is 1 year old + 1 year = 2 years old.

  So, when you arrive, the child will be 2 years old from his perspective.
